question: Which of the following is used as a fissionable fuel in a nuclear reactor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**U235**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **U235** is used as a fissionable fuel in nuclear reactors.
 
• Uranium-235 is one of the isotopes of uranium that can sustain a chain reaction of nuclear fission.
 
• It is a critical material for nuclear power generation and nuclear weapons.
 
• U235 undergoes fission when it absorbs a neutron, releasing a significant amount of energy in the form of heat and radiation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plutonium-239 (Pu239)** is another fissionable material used in nuclear reactors and weapons, although it is not mentioned in the given options.
 
• **Uranium-238 (U238)** is not fissionable by thermal neutrons but can be converted into plutonium-239 through neutron capture and subsequent beta decay.
 
• Uranium-235 makes up about **0.72% of natural uranium**, with the remainder being mostly uranium-238.
 
• The enrichment process is used to increase the concentration of U235 in uranium to make it suitable for use in reactors or weapons.
